title: Garments and fit
summary: Four sweaters in rising order of construction difficulty, each fitted to your measured body.
intro: Optional elective. It is not part of the required path, and nothing required waits on it. Garments are about measurement more than stitches. Every sweater uses the same fit loop: measure, choose a size from the schematic and ease, swatch and block, check gauge again after 4 in (10 cm) of real fabric, and fix fit before seaming. Doll clothes in TOY 310 use a small version of the same thinking.
outcomes: You can choose a size from a schematic and state the ease it gives you.
You can make a cardigan, a seamed pullover, a panel sweater with worked-on edges and a top-down sweater, each within 1 in (2.5 cm) of your planned measurements.
You can keep a fit notebook complete enough to serve as a fit specification for design work.
assessment: Each garment passes on its measured pass list. The fit notebook (7.5) is checked for completeness.

7.6: Yoke depth and body length match your planned numbers within 1/2 in (12 mm)
Your fit notebook lists each adjustment with the measurement before and after it
The sweater is recorded in your fit notebook
